recent_posts.title: ATHR: How AI Is Changing Voice Phishing
recent_posts.summary: ATHR is a new AI-powered platform that automates Telephone-Oriented Attack Delivery (TOAD) attacks by consolidating the entire attack chain into a single system. Unlike traditional vishing setups requiring multiple tools, ATHR handles lure creation, email delivery, callback routing, AI-driven social engineering, and real-time credential capture from one dashboard. Advertised on underground forums for $4,000 plus 10% commission, it supports impersonation of major services like Google, Microsoft, and Coinbase. The platform lowers the barrier to entry for voice phishing attacks, making them easier to scale and harder to detect since they bypass traditional email security filters that scan for links or attachments.

recent_posts.title: Fake GitHub Repositories Spread Malware After Claude Code Leak
recent_posts.summary: Threat actors are exploiting the accidental Claude Code source code leak by publishing fake GitHub repositories that distribute Vidar infostealer malware. On March 31, Anthropic accidentally published an npm package containing a JavaScript source map that exposed nearly the entire TypeScript codebase. While Anthropic confirmed no customer data or credentials were leaked, the incident drew widespread developer attention. Attackers capitalized on this by creating fake repositories claiming to host the leaked code or enterprise-unlocked versions, which instead deliver compressed archives containing Vidar malware. The malware harvests browser credentials, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet data, and may also proxy network traffic for persistent access. Users are warned to avoid unofficial sources and verify repositories before running any executables.

recent_posts.title: Critical Langflow Vulnerability Allows Remote Code Execution
recent_posts.summary: CISA has flagged CVE-2026-33017, a critical RCE vulnerability (CVSS 9.3) in Langflow, the open-source low-code AI agent framework. The flaw exists in the POST /api/v1/build_public_tmp/{flow_id}/flow endpoint, which passes attacker-controlled flow data directly to Python's exec() function without sandboxing or authentication checks. A single crafted HTTP request is enough to compromise exposed instances. Successful exploitation could expose API keys for cloud providers, AI platforms, and code repositories, enabling lateral movement, database access, or supply chain attacks via CI/CD pipelines. The issue is fixed in Langflow version 1.9.0, and immediate upgrades are strongly advised.

recent_posts.title: Aardvark: OpenAI’s GPT‑5-Powered Security Tool
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI launched Aardvark, a GPT-5-powered autonomous security tool that discovers and addresses software vulnerabilities at scale. Unlike traditional fuzzing or composition analysis, Aardvark uses LLM reasoning to analyze code repositories, create threat models, monitor commits, and validate vulnerabilities in sandboxed environments. In benchmark tests, it identified 92% of known vulnerabilities and discovered multiple CVEs in open-source projects. The tool integrates with GitHub and Codex, automatically generating patch proposals for human review. Currently in beta with select partners.

recent_posts.title: Windows Native AI Suite Vulnerable to Living-off-the-Land Attacks
recent_posts.summary: Security researcher hxr1 demonstrated how attackers can exploit Windows' native AI capabilities using Living-off-the-Land (LOTL) techniques. The attack hides malicious code inside ONNX model files—a legitimate machine learning format—by embedding payloads in metadata, model components, or weights using steganography. Because these files are signed by Microsoft and treated as benign by default, they evade many endpoint detection systems. Attackers can distribute poisoned models through phishing emails or open-source hubs. Recommended mitigations include adapting security tools to scan AI model files, configuring EDRs to monitor model loading processes, implementing YARA rules for static analysis, and using application controls like AppLocker.

recent_posts.title: DropPitch: AI-Driven Attacks in the Semiconductor Race
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI disrupted a Chinese-linked threat group (UNK_DropPitch) that used ChatGPT to craft phishing campaigns targeting Taiwan's semiconductor industry. The actors attempted to upgrade their command-and-control infrastructure, automate email generation, and obfuscate exploits using AI assistance. Despite leveraging AI tools, their attacks showed poor technical execution with incoherent phishing emails and mismatched content. OpenAI disabled associated accounts and shared threat indicators with security partners, highlighting both the potential and limitations of AI-assisted cyberattacks in geopolitical conflicts.

recent_posts.title: CamoLeak Vulnerability Found in GitHub Copilot Chat
recent_posts.summary: Legit Security discovered CamoLeak, a critical vulnerability (CVSS 9.6) in GitHub Copilot Chat that enabled silent data exfiltration from private repositories. The attack used prompt injection hidden in invisible PR comments, bypassing GitHub's Camo security feature by encoding sensitive data into pixel image sequences. When victims asked Copilot to explain pull requests, the injected commands executed, leaking credentials and API keys character-by-character through image requests. GitHub patched the vulnerability by disabling image rendering in Copilot Chat.

recent_posts.title: Google Drive Rolls Out AI-Powered Ransomware Protection
recent_posts.summary: Google Drive for desktop now includes AI-powered ransomware detection that monitors file activity for malicious encryption attempts. When suspicious behavior is detected, the system automatically pauses syncing and alerts users via desktop and email, allowing them to restore files to previous safe states. The AI model is trained on millions of ransomware samples and continuously adapts using threat intelligence from VirusTotal. The feature is rolling out in open beta at no extra cost for most Google Workspace commercial plans, with admin controls available through the Admin console.

recent_posts.title: ShadowLeak Vulnerability in ChatGPT Deep Research
recent_posts.summary: Security researchers discovered ShadowLeak, a zero-click vulnerability in ChatGPT's Deep Research agent that allows attackers to steal personal data through malicious HTML emails. The attack uses hidden prompt injection instructions to make the AI agent extract PII from Gmail and send it to attacker-controlled servers. OpenAI has since patched the vulnerability, but similar attacks could target other AI agents with external tool access.

recent_posts.title: 116GB of User Data Exposed in Vyro AI Breach
recent_posts.summary: Vyro AI, the company behind popular AI apps like Imagine AI Art Generator and Chatly with over 150 million downloads, suffered a major data breach exposing 116GB of user data. The exposed server contained live logs with user prompts, authentication tokens, and user agents from both production and development environments. The breach was accessible for months after being indexed in February, potentially allowing attackers to perform account takeovers and access private chat histories and generated content.
